'''Kanbara Shrine''' (神原神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Kamochō|ja|加茂町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamochō|1=kamochou|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11398866}}, {{ill|Unnan|en|Unnan|qid=Q877935|lt=Unnan City|1=Unnan}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture|1=Shimane Prefecture}}. It is known for the discovery of a {{ill|triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}} with the inscription "Jingchu 3rd Year" during the excavation of an ancient Kofun on its former grounds.
== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi|1=Ōkuninushi}}, {{ill|Iwatsutsunoo|ja|磐筒男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwatsutsunoo|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and Iwatsutsume-no-Mikoto. 
The earliest record appears in the {{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, under the entry for Kanbara-go in Ōhara District. Initially, it is believed that only Ōkuninushi was worshipped {{why|date=2022}}. However, the 1708 document ''Kanbara Shrine Engi'' compiled by Hirozawa Urushihiro, the priest of {{ill|Mito Tenmangū|ja|三刀屋天満宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mito Tenmangū|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, lists the deities as Iwatsutsunoo and Iwatsutsume-no-Mikoto.
== History ==
The ''{{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' refers to the shrine as "Kanbara Shrine," stating that it belonged to the {{ill|Department of Divinities|en|Department of Divinities|qid=Q2264720|lt=Department of Divinities|1=Department of Divinities}}. The record also describes Kanbara-go as "the place where the treasures of the Heavenly Grand deity (Ōkuninushi) are stored." 
The {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}} lists the shrine as "Kanbara Shrine." Various names have appeared over time, including "Kanbara Matsui Daimyōjin" (1611) on a ridgepole inscription, "Kanbara Shrine Matsui Daimyōjin" in the ''Kanbara Shrine Engi,'' and "Shinpo Myōjin" in the 1717 ''Un'yōshi.''
In December 1871, the shrine was Ranked as a village shrine. The current structure was relocated in 1972 due to flood control work on the {{ill|Akagawa River (Unnan City)|ja|赤川 (雲南市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagawa River (Unnan City)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} within the {{ill|Hii River|en|Hii River|qid=Q11500714|lt=Hii River system|1=Hii River}}.
== Kanbara Shrine Kofun ==
[[File:kambarajinjakofunsekisitsu.JPG|thumb|right|Reconstructed stone chamber of Kanbara Shrine Kofun]]
[[File:神原神社古墳出土 三角縁神獣鏡 (複製).JPG|thumb|180px|right|Replica of a triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror<br />{{small|Exhibited at the {{ill|National Museum of Japanese History|en|National Museum of Japanese History|qid=Q3330690|lt=National Museum of Japanese History|1=National Museum of Japanese History}}.}}]]
The shrine's former grounds were situated atop an ancient Kofun ([[kofun]]). The mound is a {{ill|square tumulus|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, estimated to measure 29 meters by 25 meters and approximately 5 meters in height. It is among the oldest kofun in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture|1=Shimane Prefecture}}, dating to the early period.
During flood control work in 1972, the shrine was moved approximately 50 meters southwest, and the kofun was excavated. Artifacts found in the [[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|Pit-style stone chamber]] included a "Jingchu 3rd Year" (239 CE) {{ill|triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/triangular-rimmed divine beast mirror|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}}, identified as a relic of the {{ill|Three Kingdoms period|ja|三国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Kingdoms period|1=Three Kingdoms period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11354714}}. These artifacts are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}, housed at the {{ill|Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo|en|Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo|qid=Q4802099|lt=Shimane Prefectural Ancient Izumo History Museum|1=Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo}}. The stone chamber has been reconstructed east of the relocated shrine and is open for public viewing.
== Festivals ==
The annual festival held on November 9 includes a lion dance, designated as an {{ill|Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県指定文化財一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture|1=Q11476462|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11476462}}. Rituals are also conducted during the {{ill|Kamiari Festival|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Kannazuki|qid=Q6364021}} period.
